symptom:
A small TCP key-value server (server/main.go) appends every PUT as a checksummed key=value line to data/kv.log, fsyncs, and only then answers OK. On start it reads the log back, verifies each record and rebuilds its in-memory map. The client remembers every PUT that was answered OK and reads them all back at the end. Directory entries are modelled strictly: a created file or directory survives a crash only after its parent directory was fsynced.

Observed on seed 2: the server was crashed and restarted four times (once during a disk operation). The client reported: acknowledged write lost: k0=v0, server now answers "NONE". The server never logged an error.

Expected: every PUT that returned OK must be readable after any number of crashes and restarts.
